passages.text: As God’s fellow workers, then, we urge you not to receive God’s grace in vain.
passages.sermon: We work together with God.\r\nWe urge you.\r\nDo not receive God’s grace in vain.
passages.original: Συνεργοῦντες δὲ καὶ παρακαλοῦμεν μὴ εἰς κενὸν τὴν χάριν τοῦ Θεοῦ δέξασθαι ὑμᾶς

passages.text: For He says: “In the time of favor I heard you, and in the day of salvation I helped you.” Behold, now is the time of favor; now is the day of salvation!
passages.sermon:
God speaks these words.
God says, “I listened to you at the right time.”
God says, “I helped you on the day of salvation.”
Now is the right time.
Now is the time when God shows favor.
Now is the day of salvation.
passages.original: λέγει γάρ Καιρῷ δεκτῷ ἐπήκουσά σου καὶ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ σωτηρίας ἐβοήθησά σοι Ἰδοὺ νῦν καιρὸς εὐπρόσδεκτος ἰδοὺ νῦν ἡμέρα σωτηρίας

passages.text: We put no obstacle in anyone’s way, so that no one can discredit our ministry.
passages.sermon: We serve God as His ministers.\r\nWe do not put any obstacle in anyone’s way.\r\nWe act so that no one can discredit our ministry.
passages.original: Μηδεμίαν ἐν μηδενὶ διδόντες προσκοπήν ἵνα μὴ μωμηθῇ ἡ διακονία

passages.text: Rather, as servants of God we commend ourselves in every way: in great endurance; in troubles, hardships, and calamities; in beatings, imprisonments, and riots; in labor, sleepless nights, and hunger; in purity, knowledge, patience, and kindness; in the Holy Spirit and in sincere love; in truthful speech and in the power of God; with the weapons of righteousness in the right hand and in the left; through glory and dishonor, slander and praise; viewed as imposters, yet genuine; as unknown, yet well-known; dying, and yet we live on; punished, yet not killed; sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; poor, yet making many rich; having nothing, and yet possessing everything.
passages.sermon:
We are servants of God.
We show ourselves in every way.
We show great endurance.
We endure troubles.
We endure hardships.
We endure calamities.
We suffer beatings.
We are put in prison.
We face riots.
We work hard.
We stay awake through sleepless nights.
We go hungry.
We live in purity.
We have knowledge.
We show patience.
We show kindness.
We have the Holy Spirit.
We love sincerely.
We speak the truth.
We have the power of God.
We use the weapons of righteousness in our right hand.
We use the weapons of righteousness in our left hand.
We go through glory.
We go through dishonor.
We face slander.
We receive praise.
People see us as imposters.
But we are genuine.
People see us as unknown.
But we are well-known.
People see us as dying.
But we live on.
People see us as punished.
But we are not killed.
People see us as sorrowful.
But we always rejoice.
People see us as poor.
But we make many rich.
People see us as having nothing.
But we possess everything.
passages.original: ἀλλ’ ἐν παντὶ συνιστάνοντες ἑαυτοὺς ὡς Θεοῦ διάκονοι ἐν ὑπομονῇ πολλῇ ἐν θλίψεσιν ἐν ἀνάγκαις ἐν στενοχωρίαις ἐν πληγαῖς ἐν φυλακαῖς ἐν ἀκαταστασίαις ἐν κόποις ἐν ἀγρυπνίαις ἐν νηστείαις ἐν ἁγνότητι ἐν γνώσει ἐν μακροθυμίᾳ ἐν χρηστότητι ἐν Πνεύματι Ἁγίῳ ἐν ἀγάπῃ ἀνυποκρίτῳ ἐν λόγῳ ἀληθείας ἐν δυνάμει Θεοῦ διὰ τῶν ὅπλων τῆς δικαιοσύνης τῶν δεξιῶν καὶ ἀριστερῶν διὰ δόξης καὶ ἀτιμίας διὰ δυσφημίας καὶ εὐφημίας ὡς πλάνοι καὶ ἀληθεῖς ὡς ἀγνοούμενοι καὶ ἐπιγινωσκόμενοι ὡς ἀποθνήσκοντες καὶ ἰδοὺ ζῶμεν ὡς παιδευόμενοι καὶ μὴ θανατούμενοι ὡς λυπούμενοι ἀεὶ δὲ χαίροντες ὡς πτωχοὶ πολλοὺς δὲ πλουτίζοντες ὡς μηδὲν ἔχοντες καὶ πάντα κατέχοντες

passages.text: We have spoken freely to you, Corinthians. Our hearts are open wide.
passages.sermon:
We are speaking to you, Corinthians.
We speak openly to you.
Our hearts are open to you.
We show you great affection.
passages.original: Τὸ στόμα ἡμῶν ἀνέῳγεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς Κορίνθιοι ἡ καρδία ἡμῶν πεπλάτυνται

passages.text: It is not our affection, but yours, that is restrained.
passages.sermon: We do not restrain our affection for you.\r\nYou restrain your own affection.
passages.original: οὐ στενοχωρεῖσθε ἐν ἡμῖν στενοχωρεῖσθε δὲ ἐν τοῖς σπλάγχνοις ὑμῶν

passages.text: As a fair exchange, I ask you as my children: Open wide your hearts also.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Corinthians.
Paul speaks to them as a spiritual father.
Paul has opened his heart to them.
Paul asks for a fair exchange.
Paul says, “I speak to you as my children.”
Paul urges them, “Open your hearts also.”
passages.original: τὴν δὲ αὐτὴν ἀντιμισθίαν ὡς τέκνοις λέγω πλατύνθητε καὶ ὑμεῖς

passages.text: Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers. For what partnership can righteousness have with wickedness? Or what fellowship does light have with darkness?
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to Christians in Corinth.
Paul tells them not to join closely with unbelievers.
He warns them not to be unequally yoked with those who do not believe.
Righteousness and wickedness cannot share partnership.
Light and darkness cannot have fellowship.
passages.original: Μὴ γίνεσθε ἑτεροζυγοῦντες ἀπίστοις τίς γὰρ μετοχὴ δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ ἀνομίᾳ ἢ τίς κοινωνία φωτὶ πρὸς σκότος

passages.text: What harmony is there between Christ and Belial? Or what does a believer have in common with an unbeliever?
passages.sermon:
Christ is the Son of God.
Belial is a name for evil or for Satan.
Christ and Belial are completely different.
There is no harmony between Christ and Belial.
A believer trusts in Christ.
An unbeliever does not trust in Christ.
A believer and an unbeliever do not share the same faith.
A believer and an unbeliever do not have true spiritual unity.
passages.original: τίς δὲ συμφώνησις Χριστοῦ πρὸς Βελιάρ ἢ τίς μερὶς πιστῷ μετὰ ἀπίστου

passages.text: What agreement can exist between the temple of God and idols? For we are the temple of the living God. As God has said: “I will dwell with them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be My people.”
passages.sermon:
The temple of God is holy.
Idols are false and unclean.
There can be no agreement between the temple of God and idols.
We are the temple of the living God.
God has spoken about us.
God said, “I will live among them.”
God said, “I will walk among them.”
God said, “I will be their God.”
God said, “They will be my people.”
passages.original: τίς δὲ συνκατάθεσις ναῷ Θεοῦ μετὰ εἰδώλων ἡμεῖς γὰρ ναὸς Θεοῦ ἐσμεν ζῶντος καθὼς εἶπεν ὁ Θεὸς ὅτι Ἐνοικήσω ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐμπεριπατήσω καὶ ἔσομαι αὐτῶν Θεός καὶ αὐτοὶ ἔσονταί μου λαός

passages.text: “Therefore come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord. Touch no unclean thing, and I will receive you.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord speaks to His people.
He commands them to come out from among unbelievers.
He tells them to be separate from those who do not believe.
He says, “Do not touch anything unclean.”
He promises, “I will receive you.”
passages.original: Διὸ ἐξέλθατε ἐκ μέσου αὐτῶν καὶ ἀφορίσθητε λέγει Κύριος καὶ ἀκαθάρτου μὴ ἅπτεσθε κἀγὼ εἰσδέξομαι ὑμᾶς

passages.text: And: “I will be a Father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord Almighty speaks.
The Lord Almighty promises a relationship.
The Lord Almighty says, “I will be a Father to you.”
You will be My sons.
You will be My daughters.”
passages.original: Καὶ Ἔσομαι ὑμῖν εἰς Πατέρα καὶ ὑμεῖς ἔσεσθέ μοι εἰς υἱοὺς καὶ θυγατέρας λέγει Κύριος Παντοκράτωρ
